rows.title: October 2026
rows.body: October was narrow and oil-led: only 4 of 19 assets rose in rupees, and the regime reads Mixed, with credit and sector leadership turning defensive.

rows.title: Regime: Mixed, leaning defensive
rows.body: Three of six votes were risk-on: copper/gold (+5.7% over 3 months), Midcap 150/FMCG (+2.6%) and equal-weight/cap-weight S&P 500 (+0.5%). Three were defensive: high yield/Treasuries (−1.8%), cyclical sectors lagging defensives (US −7.5pp, India −3.7pp over 3 months), and the US high-yield spread widening 0.59pp to 3.44%. Bonds & cash was the only family with a positive average return (+0.7%); global equity (−4.1%) and crypto (−8.2%) were weakest. Fed net liquidity fell 1.4% over 3 months to $5,746bn, and Global M2 growth slowed to +4.8% annualised over 3 months from +8.5% year on year.

rows.title: Persistence: one durable leader
rows.body: Brent crude is the only risk asset in the top 5 on both 1-month and 3-month returns, up 41.0% over 3 months. INR cash is the other persistent leader, which in a month when 15 of 19 assets fell reflects weakness elsewhere rather than strength. Emerging markets (−5.2% over 3 months) and silver (−15.2%) are persistent laggards. Leadership turned over: only 2 of September's top 5 stayed there, and the rank correlation with September was +0.09, so this month's order bore little relation to last month's. US long Treasuries and the Nifty 50 each climbed 13 places; Bitcoin fell 15 and the Nasdaq 100 fell 13.

rows.title: Divergences: credit and AI hardware
rows.body: Credit is weaker than equities: the high-yield spread widened 0.59pp over 3 months while the S&P 500 still returned +0.9% in rupees over the same period. AI hardware and Indian IT moved apart sharply: semiconductors (SMH) fell 15.0% in rupees while Nifty IT rose 18.1%, a 33.1pp gap. There was no liquidity divergence: global equities (−2.2% over 3 months) fell alongside Fed net liquidity and G3 central-bank assets. The VIX rose 3.1 points to 19.4, but equities fell too, so prices and fear agreed.

rows.title: Currency: a small headwind this month
rows.body: The rupee strengthened 0.9% in October (USD/INR 94.94), trimming rupee returns on dollar assets by about 0.9pp. Over 12 months the rupee has weakened 7.0%, which has added to the rupee return of every dollar asset over the year.

rows.title: Risks: markets price a December Fed hike
rows.body: Prediction markets, as of 27 November, put a 25bp Fed hike in December at 94% (up from 76% thirty days earlier) and no Fed cuts this year at 98%. A 25bp RBI hike is priced at 88%, but that market is thin. The largest repricings were in Bitcoin, where the odds of falling to $55,000 at some point before year-end rose from 10% to 46% and of reaching $90,000 fell from 44% to 3%, and in gold, where the odds of falling to $3,500 by December rose from 11% to 62%. A US recession by year-end is priced at 3%; an AI bubble burst by June 2027 at 36% (up 14 points). Polymarket and Kalshi agree on all 6 outcomes checked. The VIX (19.4) and India VIX (15.3) are both up over 3 months. No asset is stretched on trend.

rows.title: Positioning: some bets lean against October's moves
rows.body: Leveraged funds are the most bullish on Nasdaq 100 futures in three years (94th percentile) even though the index fell 6.7% in October, so further selling could follow if they cut those positions. Asset managers hold their smallest Treasury bond long in three years (0th percentile) while bonds rallied 5.6%. Foreign investors sold a net ₹34,843 crore of Indian equities in October, yet the Nifty 50 rose 2.0%: domestic buyers carried the market. Hedge funds are the least long on silver in three years (3rd percentile). Looking ahead, options price a Nifty move of about ±3.5% by the 29 December expiry and ±4.9% for the S&P 500 by 18 December (as of 26–27 November).

rows.title: Breadth: a narrow month
rows.body: Only 4 of 19 assets rose in rupees and 3 beat INR cash (+0.45%): Brent (+17.7%), US long Treasuries (+4.7%) and the Nifty 50 (+2.0%). The gap from best to worst was 36.6pp, Brent to silver (−18.9%). Cross-asset dispersion was 7.1%, a little above its 12-month median of 6.4%.
Credit spreads are widening and defensive sectors lead in both the US and India. Does our current risk level suit a Mixed regime?
Brent has led for three months (+41%). Is our energy and commodity exposure a deliberate position or drift?
Indian IT and global semiconductors moved 33 points apart in a month. Which side of the AI trade are we on, and through which holdings?
Markets price a December Fed hike at 94%. How exposed are our long-duration bonds and US holdings to a hike?
The rupee has weakened 7% over 12 months but strengthened in October. Should any of the dollar sleeve be hedged?
Domestic buyers absorbed ₹34,843 crore of foreign selling in October. How much do our Indian holdings depend on that domestic flow continuing?
Markets turned cautious. Our market-mood gauge slipped from risk-on in September to mixed in October, and only 4 of 19 investments rose in rupees, half as many as the month before.
Oil is the big story. Fear of a wider Iran war pushed Brent crude up 17.7% in rupees in October and 41% over three months. It is the only risk asset that has led for three months running.

Interest rates are heading up, not down. Markets give a 94% chance that the US Fed raises rates on 9 December and 88% that the RBI does on 4 December, because inflation is above both central banks' targets.

rows.body: Regime moved from Risk-on (4 of 6) to Mixed (3 of 6): high yield/Treasuries turned defensive; equal-weight/cap-weight S&P 500 turned risk-on; cyclical vs defensive sectors turned defensive.

rows.title: September
rows.body: New divergence: equities versus credit. S&P 500 3-month rupee return +0.9%; high-yield spread +0.59pp over 3 months. Equities rose while credit spreads widened sharply.
